This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f89d29e382e7d50cfe1b2a98742ac1c3d436cd26` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

git fetch origin 6f609827f6c416e46f0053357396e0989d28a90f && git checkout 6f609827f6c416e46f0053357396e0989d28a90f

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d3fa26389a1fb1098aac79a5bcfc3c4348110462`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.complete-holds-bytes.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/upload-door-ownership.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/success-envelope.conformance.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/tenant-audit-update-delete-half-repairs.test.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.metadata-outage.test.ts, packages/plugins/organizations/src/storage-upload-door-ownership.wall.test.ts, packages/plugins/organizations/src/storage-upload-organization-change.wall.test.ts + .changeset/24548-complete-holds-bytes.md, packages/spec/src/contracts/storage-service.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/local-storage-adapter.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/s3-storage-adapter.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/swappable-storage-service.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/metadata-store.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-route-ledger.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/objects/system-file.object.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-lifecycle.ts, packages/spec/src/api/storage.zod.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, .changeset/22313-chunked-completion-assembles-held-parts.md (the sibling, read at e36ee5351)

Inputs: card #24548 (body and its three comments: triage 6269100155, claim 6274788835, os-dev report 6276196635), PR #24643 (body, file list, net diff of the head against `origin/main` 7c7741dcb, merge base b12e16a56; ten files, +469/-6), and the head's check-runs. The check-runs have all concluded: the five required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) and every other run on the head are `success`; the skipped ones are path-filtered full-battery jobs (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance`, dogfood shards, `Build Docs`, the opt-in tarball smoke). No governed path and no `packages/spec/**` path is in the diff; the committed tree's changeset carries the narrowing arm, so the recogniser maps the PR to this face.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`POST {base}/upload/complete` — a completion whose key holds no bytes is refused `409` `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and the row stays `pending` (was `200`, row `committed`). Right.** `heldBytesRefusal` (storage-routes.ts:1866-1882) asks `storage.exists(file.key)`, a required `IStorageService` member (storage-service.ts), and the door sends it as `INCOMPLETE_UPLOAD_STATUS` / `INCOMPLETE_UPLOAD_CODE` (storage-routes.ts:998-1002) — the constants the chunked sibling answers from (#22313, lines 108-109), so the two completion doors give one answer to one state. It is the answer the card's expected step 4 asks for, and the premise the download doors already rest on: `isServableForDownload` serves any `committed` row unconditionally (storage-routes.ts:592-620). The message names the remedy (send the bytes to the upload URL, complete again) and no organization or key.
2. **A completion whose backend holds another number of bytes than the row's declared `size` is refused the same way; a row with no declared size, or a non-finite one, skips that leg. Right.** `getInfo(key).size` is a required contract member reported by both adapters (local `fs.stat` at local-storage-adapter.ts:263-269; S3 `HeadObject` `ContentLength` at s3-storage-adapter.ts:337-350). `FileRecord.size` is optional (metadata-store.ts:13), so the skip is "nothing to compare", not a lenient alias. The card's "compare size / eTag where the backend reports them" is met on the size.
3. **A backend fault while asking answers `500 INTERNAL` through the door's outer catch. Right on the S3 adapter and on the size leg; over-stated for the local `exists` leg.** S3 `exists` returns `false` only on `NotFound` / HTTP 404 and rethrows anything else (s3-storage-adapter.ts:322-335); both adapters' `getInfo` throw on a fault. `LocalStorageAdapter.exists`, however, folds every `fs.access` error into `false` (local-storage-adapter.ts:252-260), so a local-root fault (EACCES, ENOTDIR) at that leg is answered `409` "holds no bytes" rather than `500`. That is the adapter's pre-existing semantics, unchanged by this diff, and the outcome is a recoverable refusal (the one fault reproducible at this door, the card's own fault variant, has already failed the byte PUT, so "send the bytes" is the right remedy) — not a silent commit. The helper docblock (1858-1860) and the changeset sentence "A backend fault while asking still answers `500`" are wider than the local adapter enforces. Non-blocking; recorded for the seat in ③.
4. **Ordering: the byte check runs after `requireUploader` and `requireStartingOrganization`, before `store.updateFile`. Right.** A non-uploader gets `403` and learns nothing about where the bytes stand; an organization change keeps its `409` text; a refused file is never written, so completing again after the bytes land commits it (pinned: the wrong-size case re-PUTs and commits).
5. **The `eTag` a completion carries is stored as sent and not compared. Right within the card.** `StorageFileInfo` declares no ETag (storage-service.ts) and the S3 `getInfo` drops the `ETag` its `HeadObject` answer holds, so no adapter reports one; comparing it needs a contract member the claim excludes (`packages/spec/**`). The spec's `.describe('S3 ETag verification')` on `CompleteUploadRequestSchema.eTag` (storage.zod.ts:76) therefore stays a declared-but-unenforced claim — the dev's out-of-scope finding, escalated in ③.
6. **`GET {base}/_local/raw/:token` — a valid signed link to a key that holds no file answers `404 FILE_NOT_FOUND` (was `500 INTERNAL` "Download failed"); every other read failure keeps its `500`. Right.** The discriminator is Node's `ENOENT` and nothing else (`isMissingLocalFile`, 1890-1892); `LocalStorageAdapter.download` is `track('get', fs.readFile)` and `track` rethrows unchanged (169-187, 239-241); `SwappableStorageService.download` forwards (85-86); a non-ENOENT throw is rethrown into the existing `sendRawByteRouteFailure` (1601-1608, 1617). `FILE_NOT_FOUND` is already this family's `404` code (lines 983, 1456, 1506). The route is `server-only` in `STORAGE_ROUTE_LEDGER` (storage-route-ledger.ts:120) and the ledger carries no per-route status set, so no ledger row moves. The token is HMAC-bound to the key, so the 404 discloses nothing the link holder did not already hold.
7. **The download doors are unchanged: a `pending` row answers `404`. Right**, and now the `committed` → servable rule holds at the single-shot door on the local, swappable and S3 compositions (pinned: the refused file's `/files/:fileId/url` answers `404`, the committed one `200`).
8. **The seven existing suites: setup only, no assertion changed. Right.** Read on the diff: each adds a `storeTheBytes` / `adapter.upload` of the declared bytes before the commit it drives; the one signature change (`withRoutes`' `drive` callback gains the adapter, tenant-audit-update-delete-half-repairs.test.ts:346-364) is test-internal. These files are inside the claim's amended surface (③).
9. **Pins. Right, with two non-blocking gaps.** `storage-routes.complete-holds-bytes.test.ts` drives no-bytes / held / wrong-size-then-right through three compositions (bare local adapter, `SwappableStorageService` over local, `S3StorageAdapter` over a fake bucket whose `HeadObject` throws a `NotFound` with HTTP 404) and the raw route's 404 / 500 (EISDIR) / 200. The PR body states the red leg (8 failed / 4 passed on the unfixed file), the green leg, ablations A/B/C and a booted-wall control; the gate verdict is `Test Core` success on the head. Gaps: the raw 404 is pinned on the bare local adapter only, not through the swappable wrapper (the forwarding is read in code, item 6); a backend fault answering `500` at the commit door is claimed in prose and not pinned (item 3).
10. **Who the narrowing reaches. Right.** The SDK's `storage.upload` PUTs to `presigned.uploadUrl` (client/src/index.ts:5341) before it POSTs `upload/complete` (5355); the console's `UploadProvider` documents the same three-step order. Only a client that completes before it sends — the defect's own shape — now sees the `409`.
11. **No public surface is added: no new route, no new export, no `req.query` read (no closed-set declaration owed), no spec edit, no governed path. Right.**
12. **The acceptance note "a refused S3 upload's bytes stay in the bucket" is answered by reading:** `sys_file` declares `retention: { maxAge: '7d', onlyWhen: { status: 'pending' } }` (objects/system-file.object.ts:202) and the reap guard deletes a pending row's bytes before the row (attachment-lifecycle.ts:643). A size-mismatched object under a now-uncommittable pending row is reclaimed with it. No card owed.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/24548-complete-holds-bytes.md` bumps `@objectstack/service-storage: minor`, carries the `Clause-②:` line `no (narrowing)`, and the adr-0087 comment marker with category `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` and its reasoning. **Matches what the diff publishes.** The only published source that moves is `packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts`; the `packages/plugins/organizations` changes are test files and publish nothing, so one package bumped is right. A request the door answered `200` and now answers `409` is an accept-set narrowing — `clause2-line.mjs` defines `no (narrowing)` as exactly that, not a widening but breaking — so `patch` (the claim's original line) and `skip-changeset` are both wrong for this diff, and `minor` is the level the launch-window convention assigns a breaking change (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`). The marker category is right: no spec key, authorable spelling, export or stored shape is removed or re-shaped, and the body carries no code-rewrite prescription (its remedy is "send the bytes, complete again"). The level, arm and category are byte-for-byte the sibling's (`.changeset/22313-chunked-completion-assembles-held-parts.md` at e36ee5351, same package, same 200-to-409 shape). Gate verdicts on the head: `Check Changeset` success, `Lint & Repo Gates` success (the ADR-0087 registration and no-major gates run there).

The PR body's `Clause-②:` line, line 2, reads `no (narrowing)` — it agrees with the changeset. Two sentences of the body's prose predate the ruling commit d3fa26389 and now contradict it: "What changed" still calls the changeset `patch`, and the acceptance note still says the line was copied verbatim from the claim as `no` and that the seat decides. Neither is the line the recogniser reads, so neither carries the verdict; the body edit is escalated in ③. The commit and PR titles carry no `!` where the sibling's did; no gate reads it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1 and open question 2 (seven existing test files outside the claim's first file surface): answered, closed.** The claim (6274788835) carries the amendment — it names the five service-storage suites and the two organizations wall suites, "each storing the declared bytes first with no assertion changed", on the precedent of e36ee5351. The diff touches exactly those seven and no other path outside the declared surface; item ①.8 confirms the edits are setup only.
- **Open question 1 (`patch` + `no`, or `minor` + `no (narrowing)` with an ADR-0087 marker): answered on the head, closed.** Commit d3fa26389, authored under the seat's session, declares the narrowing and the marker; ② judges it right. Residual, escalated to the seat: edit the PR body's two stale sentences (the `patch` mention under "What changed" and the "copied verbatim from the claim" acceptance note) so the body agrees with its own line 2 and the changeset. A body edit; no new head.
- **Deviation 2 (eTag not compared, reported NOT MEASURED): right within the card (①.5). Escalated:** the dev's class-b out-of-scope finding is not filed. `CompleteUploadRequestSchema.eTag` is described as "S3 ETag verification" while the door stores it verbatim and no adapter reports a stored ETag to compare against — declared, not enforced (Prime Directive #10). The seat files it as its own card (the dev's dedupe words are in the report), outside this PR.
- **Deviation 3 (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` not measured locally): answered by the head's `Lint & Repo Gates` success.** Closed.
- **Deviation 4 (`origin/main` moved after the merge; not re-merged): closed.** The check-runs ran on the merge of the head into base 14ccb1da; `main` is 7c7741dcb at this reading; the intervening commits the dev names touch metadata-protocol, plugin-approvals and docs, none of this diff's packages; the queue rebuilds the PR onto current `main` (§7) and that is where joint breakage would surface.
- **Deviations 5 and 6 (attribution in AGENTS.md's form; ablation B's refused first attempt, rerun): recorded, nothing owed.**
- **Acceptance note on refused S3 bytes: answered in ①.12, nothing owed.**
- **My own flag, non-blocking:** the changeset sentence and helper docblock stating that a backend fault while asking answers `500` are wider than `LocalStorageAdapter.exists` enforces (①.3). The behaviour that ships is a recoverable `409` with the right remedy for the fault reproducible at this door, so this record does not hold the PR on it; it is recorded here so the seat reads the changelog sentence with that qualification.
- **Docs drift advisory (PR comment 6276167267): closed.** It lists `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx` on the `FILE_NOT_FOUND` literal; that page's line 168 states the download doors' `404` in a record payload, not the raw byte route, and nothing on it is falsified by this diff.
- **Landing:** no governed surface, so this record is owed by the narrowing face alone; the PR is draft with auto-merge unarmed, every required context is green on the head, and the owning seat readies it and lets the queue land it.
